name: Erl
kurzbeschreibung: A cultural and artistic hub in the Inntal valley, home to the world-famous Tiroler Festspiele Erl and the tradition of Passionsspiele.
title: Erl
metaDescription: Erl in Tyrol's Lower Inn Valley: Oldest passion play village, Tyrolean Festival Erl, futuristic festival hall, Blaue Quelle spring and Mount Kranzhorn.
text:
Overview

Erl is situated at an elevation of 476 meters in the Lower Inn Valley in the district of Kufstein, directly on the Bavarian border adjacent to Oberaudorf and Flintsbach am Inn. Home to approximately 1,600 residents, this vibrant cultural community expands across an open valley floor between the Zahmer Kaiser and the Chiemgau Alps. Internationally celebrated as the oldest Passion Play community in the German-speaking world and as the home of the Tyrolean Festival Erl, the village features a striking architectural pair: the iconic historic Passion Play Theatre and the futuristic Festival Hall, seamlessly bridging deep-rooted Tyrolean heritage with world-class arts and natural wonders.

History

Human settlement around Erl dates back to Roman antiquity, verified by an inscribed third-century Roman Mithras stone preserved in the parish church of Saint Andrew. The village was first documented in 788 AD in the goods register of Archbishop Arn of Salzburg. Following the Landshut War of Succession in 1504 under Emperor Maximilian I, Erl became permanently integrated into Tyrol. The village's defining cultural legacy is the Erl Passion Play: founded upon a solemn plague vow, it was first recorded in 1613, giving Erl the oldest Passion Play tradition in the German-speaking realm. Staged every six years, approximately 600 local amateurs—nearly a third of the entire township—perform the life and Passion of Christ, recognized as UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage in 2013. In 1959, architect Robert Schuller completed the acoustically celebrated, whitewashed Passion Play Theatre. In 1997, conductor Gustav Kuhn established the Tyrolean Festival Erl, culminating in 2012 with the inauguration of the striking geometric Festival Hall designed by Delugan Meissl Associated Architects.

Getting There

By automobile from Germany, Erl is accessed completely toll-free without an Austrian motorway vignette via motorway A93, exiting at Oberaudorf and driving just three kilometers across the border. From Austria, travelers take motorway A12 to the Kufstein Nord exit, proceeding along regional highways through Niederndorf directly into Erl. Rail passengers arrive at nearby Oberaudorf station in Bavaria or the major railway hub Kufstein in Tyrol, which connects directly to Munich, Innsbruck, and Vienna. VVT regional bus line 4030 runs regular scheduled services from Kufstein station to Erl. Special festival shuttle buses operate directly between Kufstein railway station and the performance halls during concert seasons.

Tips

Experiencing opera or symphonic concerts during the Tyrolean Festival Erl or attending the historic Passion Play is an exceptional cultural highlight. Nature lovers should visit the Blaue Quelle, Tyrol's oldest registered natural monument and its most powerful karst spring, pumping over 700 liters of pristine emerald-tinted water per second, situated beside an acclaimed gourmet restaurant. Hikers can summit Mount Kranzhorn (1,368 m), famously crowned by two adjacent summit crosses along the border ridge—one Bavarian and one Tyrolean. Wind sports enthusiasts marvel at the Erler Wind, an intriguing local meteorological phenomenon where cool mountain air funnels powerfully through the narrow valley opening into the Bavarian plains.
